title: Yes, I developed my game with the help of AI. And so should you.
author: BrassberryFarms
selftext:
I have been a professional software engineer for 7 years now. I have real world experience writing code for production level applications that serve millions of users, and I can tell you confidently, AI is an exceptionally powerful tool, and it isn’t going anywhere. 

To start, most humans are terrible at coding. Memory leaks, inefficient code, limitations of feature building, are all serious problems humans face when writing code. We’re even worse at finding the causes and fixing them. AI is not perfect, but it can help solve anything that code can cause.

The term “AI slop” does nothing except hold everyone back. AI is the great equalizer. Suddenly, solo game developers hold the power to make games that meet or exceed the potential of games that would cost millions to make. We should all be happy this is a new tool in our tool belt and work to use it as effectively as possible. 

So what about the AI slop? It’s true that many games that are made with AI are terrible. It’s also true that AI has lowered the bar for the technical skills and timeline required to build a game. But “slop” is not unique to AI. Humans push out slop at a far higher rate, AI only amplified their ability to actually get it to a complete state that can be published. 

The issue is the people behind it. The people with no vision who do little to no testing of their games before clicking publish, and who don’t understand what actually makes a game fun. In the hands of a developer who has the attention to detail, the dedication to sit and play test for 100s of hours in order to iron out bugs and tweak their games to make them more fun, and the patience to wait until a game is truly ready before publishing, AI is an incredibly powerful tool. 

I don’t understand the AI witch hunt going on. I think that at best, the sentiment is misplaced and we should really be more concerned about lazy developers who don’t test their games properly. But I have been building games with Unity for almost a decade, and with the help of AI I’m finally able to build the games I could only dream of before.

comments.author: Fate_Drawn
comments.body: I totally agree. I have been playing games for years and AI gave me the opportunity to develop something myself. It’s fun to make a game and when you see people really playing it, it makes it even better!

comments.author: bolharr2250
comments.body: If you don't understand why folks don't like AI it seems like you're deliberately ignoring the environmental and societal impacts people have a massive issue with, not to mention the sacredness of human creativity that it defiles.
